ps-union-overlap-01: 'At least one of the two' matlab Python ya Statistics ya dono — yaani union $|P\cup S|$. Dhyan do: 12 students dono lists mein gine gaye hain.
Rule: $|P\cup S|=|P|+|S|-|P\cap S|$, yahan $|P|=35$, $|S|=28$, $|P\cap S|=12$. Total 60 is sawaal mein seedha kaam nahi aata.
Pehle $35+28=63$ — isme 'both' wale 12 do baar gine gaye. Ab overlap sirf ek baar ghatao; do baar ghatane se 'exactly one' milta hai, aur $60-$union 'neither' hai.
ps-union-overlap-02: 'Neither A nor B' = na A, na B. Ye union ka complement hai: $P(A^c\cap B^c)=1-P(A\cup B)$.
Pehle $0.45+0.35=0.80$; ab overlap 0.15 sirf ek baar ghatao to union milega. Trap: union pe hi ruk jaana — wo 'at least one' hai, 'neither' uska complement hai.
ps-union-overlap-03: 'Divisible by 4 or by 6' ek union hai. Jo numbers dono se divisible hain (jaise 12, 24) wo dono lists mein aayenge — unhe ek hi baar ginna hai.
Count $=\lfloor300/4\rfloor+\lfloor300/6\rfloor-(\text{dono se divisible})$. Dono se divisible = lcm$(4,6)$ ke multiples.
$\lfloor300/4\rfloor=75$, $\lfloor300/6\rfloor=50$. Trap: overlap ke liye $4\times6=24$ mat lo — lcm$(4,6)=12$ hai; ab $\lfloor300/12\rfloor$ nikal ke formula lagao.
ps-union-overlap-04: 'None of the three' $=100-|A\cup B\cup C|$. Teen sets hain, to pairwise overlaps aur triple overlap dono chahiye.
$|A\cup B\cup C|=(50+40+30)-(15+10+12)+5$. Triple overlap 5 ko wapas add karna hai, ghataana nahi.
Singles ka sum $=120$, pairwise ka sum $=37$. Trap: 120 > 100 dekh ke 'sab covered' maan lena, ya $+5$ bhool jaana; union nikaal ke 100 se ghatao.
ps-union-overlap-05: $P(A)+P(B)=1.1$ — ye 1 se zyada hai. Socho: kya dono events bina kisi overlap ke reh sakte hain?
Rule: $P(A\cap B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cup B)=1.1-P(A\cup B)$, aur $P(A\cup B)$ hamesha $\le1$ aur $\ge\max(0.6,0.5)$.
$P(A\cup B)$ ki max value 1 aur min 0.6 rakh ke overlap ki range nikalo, phir har option us range se check karo. Trap: $0.6\times0.5$ — wo independence maanta hai, jo given nahi.
ps-sampling-no-replace-01: 'Without replacement' — pehli red nikalne ke baad box mein 7 balls bachti hain, aur red sirf 4.
Sequential route: $P(R_1)\cdot P(R_2\mid R_1)$. Ya combinations: (5 red mein se 2 chunne ke tarike)/(8 mein se 2 chunne ke tarike). Ek hi route rakho.
$P(R_1)=\frac58$. Ab doosri draw ke waqt kitni red aur kitni total bachi? Trap: $(5/8)^2$ lena — wo replacement hai; aur $\binom52$ ko $8\cdot7$ se divide karna routes mix karna hai.
ps-sampling-no-replace-02: 'Exactly 2 white' in 3 draws = 2 white + 1 black, kisi bhi order mein. Without replacement hai, to binomial nahi chalega.
Combinations route: $\binom62\binom41/\binom{10}3$. Neeche ke numbers $2+1=3$, upar ke $6+4=10$.
$\binom62=15$, $\binom41=4$; ab $\binom{10}3$ nikal ke divide karo. Trap: sirf W,W,B order ka $\frac6{10}\cdot\frac59\cdot\frac48$ lena — black teen positions pe aa sakta hai.
ps-sampling-no-replace-03: Do cards bina wapas rakhe — pehla ace nikalne ke baad deck mein 51 cards aur 3 aces bachte hain.
Sequential: $\frac{4}{52}\cdot\frac{3}{51}$; ya combinations: $\binom42/\binom{52}2$. Dono same result denge, bas route mix mat karo.
$\frac4{52}=\frac1{13}$; ab $\frac3{51}$ simplify karke multiply karo. Trap: $4\cdot3=12$ ko $\binom{52}2=1326$ se divide karna (ordered upar, unordered neeche), ya $(4/52)^2$ lena.
ps-sampling-no-replace-04: 'Both faulty within first 3 tests' ka matlab: pehle 3 tested bulbs mein dono faulty shaamil hain — kis test number pe mile, ye matter nahi karta.
Unordered route: pehle 3 bulbs ko 6 mein se ek 3-subset socho. $P=\binom22\binom41/\binom63$.
$\binom22=1$, $\binom41=4$; ab $\binom63$ nikalo. Trap: sirf 'tests 1 aur 2 pe faulty' ginna — pair tests (1,3) ya (2,3) pe bhi ho sakta hai.
ps-hypergeometric-01: Log bina replacement chune jaate hain, isliye Binomial(4, 0.4) nahi — ye hypergeometric hai. Exactly 2 women matlab baaki 2 men.
$P=\binom42\binom62/\binom{10}4$: 4 women mein se 2, 6 men mein se 2, total 10 mein se 4.
$\binom42=6$, $\binom62=15$; ab $\binom{10}4$ nikal ke divide karo. Trap: men wala factor $\binom62$ bhool jaana.
ps-hypergeometric-02: 'At least one defective' — 1, 2, 3 defective ke cases jodne se aasaan hai complement: sample mein koi defective nahi.
$P(\ge1)=1-\binom{15}3/\binom{20}3$; yahan 15 = non-defective items, aur sampling bina replacement hai.
$\binom{15}3=455$, $\binom{20}3=1140$; ratio nikalo aur 1 se ghatao. Trap: ratio $P(\text{none})$ pe hi ruk jaana, ya $1-0.75^3$ (replacement wala) lena.
ps-hypergeometric-03: 4 balls bina replacement, order irrelevant: 2 red 7 mein se aur 2 green 5 mein se aane chahiye.
$\binom{12}4=495$. Ab $\binom72$ aur $\binom52$ nikalo — trap: $\binom72$ mein $7\cdot6$ ko 2 se divide karna mat bhoolna. Binomial(4, 7/12) bhi galat hai.
ps-hypergeometric-04: Selection bina replacement hai: 12 mein se 4. 'Exactly 3 qualified' matlab 3 qualified (5 mein se) aur 1 unqualified (7 mein se).
Har option check karo: neeche ke numbers ka sum 4 ho, denominator bhi 4 chune, aur 7 mein se 1 wala factor ho. Trap: $(5/12)^3$ wala binomial — har pick ke baad probability badalti hai.
ps-at-least-one-01: 'At least one fails' = 1, 2 ya 3 failures. Inko alag-alag jodne ki jagah complement lo: koi bhi fail nahi.
Ek server ke fail na hone ki prob $0.9$; ab $0.9^3$ nikalo aur complement lo. Trap: $0.1+0.1+0.1$ jodna — do ya teen failures wale din double count hote hain.
ps-at-least-one-02: 'At least one six' in 4 rolls — complement socho: chaaron rolls mein ek bhi six nahi aaya.
$(5/6)^2=25/36\approx0.694$; ise square karo to $P(\text{no six})$ milega. Trap: $4\times\frac16$ jodna, ya $(5/6)^4$ pe hi ruk jaana.
ps-at-least-one-03: 'At least one success $\ge0.95$' ko complement mein socho: $n$ trials mein ek bhi success nahi — uski prob $\le0.05$ honi chahiye.
$1-0.8^n\ge0.95 \iff 0.8^n\le0.05$. Sabse chhota integer $n$ chahiye jo ye satisfy kare.
Log lo: $n\ln0.8\le\ln0.05$; dono logs negative hain, to divide karte hi sign flip: $n\ge\ln0.05/\ln0.8$. Trap: fractional value ko round down karna — final $n$ pe $0.8^n$ check karo.
ps-at-least-one-04: 'Some digit appears more than once' ke bahut cases hain (ek pair, do pair, triple...). Complement simple hai: chaaron digits alag-alag.
$P(\text{repeat})=1-\dfrac{10\cdot9\cdot8\cdot7}{10^4}$; total PINs $10^4$ kyunki repetition allowed hai.
$10\cdot9\cdot8\cdot7=5040$, to $P(\text{all distinct})=5040/10000$. Trap: isi pe ruk jaana — ye 'all distinct' hai; aur pairs ki probabilities jodna over-count karta hai.
ps-ordered-outcomes-01: Do dice distinguishable hain — (1,6) aur (6,1) alag outcomes. Sample space 36 equally likely ordered pairs ka hai, 11 sums ka nahi.
$P=\dfrac{\#\{(a,b): a+b=7\}}{36}$. Har $a$ ke liye $b=7-a$ valid (1 se 6) hai ya nahi, check karo.
$a=1\Rightarrow b=6$, $a=2\Rightarrow b=5$ — aise hi $a=6$ tak likho aur gino. Trap: sirf {1,6},{2,5},{3,4} unordered ginna — har pair ordered mein do baar aata hai.
ps-ordered-outcomes-02: 3 coins ke $2^3=8$ ordered outcomes equally likely hain. '0, 1, 2, 3 heads' wale 4 cases equally likely nahi hain.
$P=\dfrac{\#\text{outcomes with exactly 2 H}}{8}$. Exactly 2 heads = ek tail; tail ki position choose karne ke tarike gino.
HHT ek outcome hai; tail ko baaki positions pe rakh ke bache outcomes bhi likho. Trap: 'at least two' (HHH bhi shaamil) se confuse mat karo — exactly two chahiye.
ps-ordered-outcomes-03: 'Larger number exactly 4' = dono dice $\le4$, aur kam se kam ek die pe 4. 36 ordered pairs mein gino, unordered nahi.
$P(\max\le4)=16/36$ (dono dice 1–4). Ab $\max\le3$ ke outcomes nikal ke ghatao. Trap: 16/36 pe ruk jaana, ya {4,1},{4,2},... unordered gin lena.
ps-ordered-outcomes-04: 'At least 10' = sum 10, 11 ya 12. Har sum ke ordered outcomes 36 mein se gino — 11 sums equally likely nahi hain.
Sum 10: (4,6),(5,5),(6,4) — 3 outcomes. Ab 11 aur 12 ke gino. Trap: (5,6) aur (6,5) ko ek hi ginna, ya direction ulta karke 'sum $\le9$' le lena.
ps-given-restrict-01: 'Given that the sum is 8' — ab sample space sirf sum 8 wale ordered outcomes hain, poore 36 nahi.
Sum 8 ke ordered outcomes likho: (2,6),(3,5),... (6,2) tak, aur unme 6 wale gino. Trap: denominator 36 rakhna, ya {2,6},{3,5},{4,4} unordered ginna.
ps-given-restrict-02: '$A\mid B$' — B ho chuka hai, to B hi naya 'poora space' ban jaata hai. Denominator mein B aayega.
Ab bas ye ratio nikalo. Trap: $P(A)=0.5$ se divide karna — wo $P(B\mid A)$ hai; aur sirf 0.1 likhna joint probability hai, conditional nahi.
ps-given-restrict-03: 'Given at least two heads' — sample space ko sirf un outcomes tak restrict karo jinme 2 ya 3 heads hain.
$P(HHH\mid\ge2H)=\dfrac{P(HHH)}{P(\ge2H)}$; dono ko 8 ordered outcomes mein gino.
Exactly 2 heads: HHT, HTH, THH; isme HHH jodo to given set ban gaya. Trap: 'ek toss bacha, to 1/2' — condition ye fix nahi karti ki kaun se tosses heads the.
ps-given-restrict-04: 'Picked from those who bought' — ab universe sirf buyers hain, 200 customers nahi. Ye $P(\text{mobile}\mid\text{bought})$ hai.
Total buyers $=36+12$. Trap: $36/120$ — wo ulta conditional $P(\text{bought}\mid\text{mobile})$ hai; aur $36/200$ joint hai.
ps-independence-01: 'Mutually exclusive' matlab dono ek saath ho hi nahi sakte: $P(A\cap B)=0$. Isko independence se mat milao.
Rule: independent tab jab $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$; aur $P(A\mid B)=P(A\cap B)/P(B)$. Yahan $P(A)P(B)=0.12$.
Union $=0.3+0.4-0=0.7$, to 0.58 wala option $0.3\times0.4$ ghata raha hai (independence). Ab $P(A\mid B)$ bhi $P(A\cap B)=0$ daal ke nikalo.
ps-independence-02: Saare options $P(A\cap B)$ pe tike hain. Union diya hai, to pehle overlap nikalo.
$P(A\cap B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cup B)$. Phir: exclusive $\iff$ overlap $=0$; independent $\iff$ overlap $=P(A)P(B)$.
$P(A\cap B)=0.4+0.5-0.7=0.2$; ise $0.4\times0.5$ se compare karo, aur 'neither' ke liye $1-P(A\cup B)$ lo. Har option alag judge karo. Trap: overlap non-zero ko dependence samajhna.
ps-independence-03: Overlap hona dependence nahi hai. Har pair ke liye test: $P(X\cap Y)=P(X)P(Y)$? Fair die hai, to prob $=|\text{set}|/6$.
$A\cap B=\{2,4\}$, to $P(A\cap B)=2/6$; ise $\frac12\cdot\frac46$ se compare karo. Ab $A\cap C$ ke liye same karo. Trap: 'overlap hai to independent nahi' sochna.
ps-independence-04: Independent ≠ mutually exclusive: independent events overlap karte hain, to union mein seedha add nahi kar sakte.
Overlap $=0.3\times0.6=0.18$; ab ise $0.3+0.6$ se ghatao. Trap: 0.9 (exclusive maan ke) ya 0.18 (intersection) ko hi union likh dena.
ps-independence-05: Har statement ko definitions se ek-ek karke test karo. Dhyan do: $0<P(A),P(B)<1$, to koi event impossible ya certain nahi.
Rules: independent $\iff P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$; exclusive $\iff P(A\cap B)=0$. Aur $P(A\mid B)>P(A)\iff P(A\cap B)>P(A)P(B)$ — yahi $P(B\mid A)$ ke liye bhi.

Complement wale statement ke liye likho $P(A^c\cap B)=P(B)-P(A\cap B)$ aur independence lagao. Trap: independent aur exclusive ko same samajhna — positive probabilities pe independent events overlap karte hi hain.
ps-total-prob-01: Item teen machines mein se kisi ek se aaya — ye ek partition hai. Har machine ka defect rate uske output share se weight hoga.
Total probability: $P(D)=0.5(0.02)+0.3(0.03)+0.2(0.05)$ — har branch = prior × defect rate.
Pehli branch: $0.5\times0.02=0.010$. Baaki do branches nikal ke jodo. Trap: 2%, 3%, 5% ka simple average ya seedha sum lena — weights bhool gaye.
ps-total-prob-02: Coin pehle urn chunta hai, phir ball — do-stage experiment. 'Red' dono urns se aa sakta hai, to dono branches chahiye.
Urn I branch: $\frac12\cdot\frac35=0.3$. Ab urn II branch nikal ke jodo. Trap: sirf ek branch rakhna, ya $0.6\times0.2$ multiply karna — branches alternatives hain, add hoti hain.
ps-total-prob-03: B se draw karne se pehle B badal chuka hai: ab usme 9 balls hain. Moved ball white thi ya black — ye do cases (partition) hain.
Pehli branch: $\frac25\cdot\frac59=\frac{10}{45}$. Ab doosri branch nikal ke jodo. Trap: transfer ignore karke $4/8$ lena, ya maan lena ki black hi move hui.
ps-total-prob-04: Email ya spam hai ya nahi — 40/60 ka partition. 'Offer' dono classes mein aata hai, alag-alag rate se.
Spam branch: $0.4\times0.3=0.12$. Ab non-spam branch nikal ke jodo. Trap: 0.12 pe ruk jaana (sirf spam), ya 0.3 aur 0.05 ka 50/50 average lena.
ps-bayes-01: Sawaal $P(\text{affected}\mid+)$ maang raha hai — ulta conditional, 95% wala nahi. Base rate sirf 1% hai, ye bahut matter karega.
Bayes: $P(D\mid+)=\dfrac{0.01\times0.95}{0.01\times0.95+0.99\times0.05}$. Numerator = affected branch, denominator = saare positives.
Numerator $=0.0095$, false-positive branch $=0.99\times0.05=0.0495$. Ab inko jod ke $P(+)$ banao aur divide karo. Trap: 0.95 likh dena, ya numerator pe hi ruk jaana.
ps-bayes-02: 'Item is defective, came from C?' — ye $P(C\mid D)$ hai, reverse direction. Evidence (defect) aur prior (20%) dono lagenge.
Numerator $=0.2\times0.05=0.010$; denominator ke liye baaki branches $0.010$ aur $0.009$ bhi jodo. Trap: B ki branch upar rakhna, ya sirf prior 0.2 dena.
ps-bayes-03: Red ball mili; ab poochha hai urn II ki prob — $P(II\mid R)$. Priors 1/4 aur 3/4 barabar nahi hain, unhe ignore mat karna.
Urn II branch: $\frac34\times0.4=0.3$; urn I branch: $\frac14\times0.8=0.2$. Ab total nikal ke divide karo. Trap: urn I ki branch upar rakhna, ya priors chhod ke $0.4/(0.8+0.4)$.
ps-bayes-04: Fraud sirf 0.1% hai, legit 99.9%. Flag milne pe $P(\text{fraud}\mid\text{flag})$ chahiye — 99% detection rate wala ulta conditional nahi.
Bayes: $\dfrac{0.001\times0.99}{0.001\times0.99+0.999\times0.01}$. Neeche dono flag-branches ka total.
Fraud branch $=0.00099$, legit branch $=0.00999$. Ab ratio ka order of magnitude socho. Trap: 0.99 chun lena (reverse conditional), ya legit branch ko numerator mein rakhna.
ps-bayes-05: Sensitivity $=P(+\mid D)=0.9$, specificity $=P(-\mid D^c)=0.9$, to false positive rate $0.1$. Options prevalence $\pi$ badal ke poochh rahe hain.
$P(D\mid+)=\dfrac{0.9\pi}{0.9\pi+0.1(1-\pi)}$ aur $P(+)=0.9\pi+0.1(1-\pi)$. Har option mein diya $\pi$ daalo.
$\pi=0.01$: numerator $0.009$, false-positive branch $0.099$ — ab ratio ko 0.1 se compare karo. $\pi=0.5$ bhi aise hi try karo. Trap: maan lena ki prior ka asar nahi padta.
ps-pmf-moments-01: $P(X=x)=kx$ — probabilities equal nahi hain, aur $k$ unknown hai. Pehle normalise karo, phir mean.
$\sum_{x=1}^4 kx=1$ se $k$ nikalo; phir $E[X]=\sum x\cdot kx=k(1^2+2^2+3^2+4^2)$.
$k(1+2+3+4)=10k=1$, to $k=0.1$. Ab $1+4+9+16$ ko $k$ se multiply karo. Trap: 1–4 ka simple average lena, ya $k$ se multiply karna bhool jaana.
ps-pmf-moments-02: Support $x=0,1,2,3$ hai — $x=0$ bhi shaamil hai, uski prob $c(0+1)=c$ hai. Pehle normalise, phir $E[X^2]$.
Normalisation se $c=0.1$. Ab bracket wale terms jodo aur $c$ se multiply karo. Trap: $(E[X])^2$ dena — $E[X^2]$ mein values pehle square hoti hain; aur $x=0$ chhodne se $c$ galat aata hai.
ps-pmf-moments-03: $E[X^2]$ chahiye — har value ko pehle square karo, phir uski probability se weight karo. $-1$ ka square positive hota hai.
Pehla term: $(-1)^2\times0.3=+0.3$ (minus nahi). Ab teesra term jodo. Trap: $E[X]=0.7$ ka square lena, ya variance $E[X^2]-(E[X])^2$ de dena.
ps-pmf-moments-04: $X$ sirf 1 ya 3, dono 1/2 prob se. Har statement ke liye $E[X]$, $E[X^2]$, $E[1/X]$ seedha definition se nikalo.
$E[X]=\frac{1+3}{2}=2$. Ab $E[X^2]=\frac{1+9}{2}$ aur $E[1/X]=\frac{1+1/3}{2}$ nikal ke har option se milao. Trap: $E[X^2]=(E[X])^2$ ya $E[1/X]=1/E[X]$ maan lena.
ps-var-linear-01: $3X-5$ ek linear transform hai. Shift $-5$ spread ko nahi badalta; sirf scale 3 ka asar padta hai.
$a^2=9$ — ab ise $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ se multiply karo. Trap: $3\times4$ (a ka square bhoolna), ya $-5$ ko variance mein bhi lagana.
ps-var-linear-02: $E[X^2]=13$ variance nahi hai. Pehle $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ nikalo, phir linear transform ka rule lagao.
$\mathrm{Var}(X)=13-4=9$. Ab $(-2)^2$ se multiply karo — minus sign square mein gayab, aur $+7$ spread nahi badalta. Trap: 13 ko hi variance maan lena.
ps-var-linear-03: $Y=5-X$ ek linear transform hai ($a=-1$, $b=5$). Shift spread ko nahi badalta, aur SD kabhi negative nahi hota.
$|a|=|-1|=1$ — ab ise $\mathrm{SD}(X)$ se multiply karo. Trap: $5-3$ karna (shift lagana), minus sign rakhna, ya SD ki jagah variance de dena.
ps-var-linear-04: Do cheezein chahiye: $E[Y]$ (shift aur sign dono matter karte hain) aur $\mathrm{Var}(Y)$ (sirf $a^2$). $E[X^2]=5$ variance nahi hai.
$\mathrm{Var}(X)=5-1^2=4$. Ab $E[Y]$ sign dhyan se nikalo aur $\mathrm{Var}(Y)$ ke liye 9 se multiply karo. Trap: $-3$ se multiply karna (negative variance), ya 5 ko Var maan lena.
ps-var-linear-05: $F=1.8C+32$ linear hai. Mean 20 is sawaal mein kaam ka nahi — sirf variance chahiye, aur +32 spread nahi badalta.
$1.8^2=3.24$. Ab 25 se multiply karo. Trap: 1.8 se hi multiply karna (square bhoolna), ya end mein 32 jod dena.
ps-model-select-01: 'Average rate of 3 per minute, independently' aur 'number of calls in a window' — ye counts-in-an-interval model hai. Window 10 minute ki hai, 1 ki nahi.
Rate per minute hai, window minutes mein — ab multiply karke $\lambda$ nikalo. Trap: per-minute rate 3 hi rakh dena; aur Binomial ke 10 'trials' nahi hain, ek minute mein kai calls aa sakti hain.
ps-model-select-02: Key words: 'batch of 30', '6 defective', 'without replacement' — fixed finite lot se bina wapas rakhe nikalna.
Checklist: finite lot, no replacement → hypergeometric; independent trials, constant $p$ → binomial; first success tak wait → geometric; rate × interval → Poisson.
Pehla chip defective hone ki prob $6/30$; agar wo defective nikla to doosre ki $5/29$ — kya $p$ constant raha? Isi se decide karo. Trap: $6/30=0.2$ dekh ke Binomial(5, 0.2) chun lena.
ps-model-select-03: Har option pe binomial checklist lagao: fixed $n$, har trial ke do outcomes, independent trials, constant $p$.
Fail hone ke do common reasons: $n$ fixed nahi (first success tak wait → geometric), ya bina replacement ($p$ badalta hai → hypergeometric).

Die wala option: 'until the first six' mein rolls ki ginti pehle se fixed nahi — ye geometric hai. Baaki options pe bhi yahi checklist chalao. Trap: deck se 'dealt' cards ko independent trials samajhna.
ps-model-select-04: Har question pe independent guess, 4 mein se 1 sahi — fixed 20 trials, constant $p$. 'Expected number' poochha hai, koi probability nahi.
$p=1/4=0.25$ sirf ek question ke liye hai; ab 20 questions ke liye $np$ nikalo. Trap: $P(X=k)$ wala binomial formula lagana — expectation ke liye sirf $np$ chahiye.
ps-model-select-05: 12 independent rolls, har roll pe six ki prob $1/6$ — fixed $n$, constant $p$: binomial. 'Exactly two' = $P(X=2)$, mean nahi.
$\binom{12}2=\frac{12\cdot11}{2}=66$ (2 se divide karna mat bhoolo). Ab $(\frac16)^2(\frac56)^{10}$ nikal ke multiply karo. Trap: $\binom{12}2$ factor hi chhod dena.
ps-tail-direction-01: '$X\ge3$' with $n=4$ matlab $X=3$ ya $X=4$ — sirf 2 terms. Direction dhyan se: $\ge$ hai, $\le$ nahi.
$(0.5)^4=1/16$, aur $\binom43=4$. Ab $\binom44$ jodo. Trap: complement lete waqt $1-P(X\le3)$ likhna — $X\ge3$ ka complement $X\le2$ hai.
ps-tail-direction-02: '$X\ge2$' ke infinite terms hain (2, 3, 4, ...). Complement lo: $X\le1$, yaani sirf $X=0$ aur $X=1$.
$e^{-2}\approx0.1353$, to $P(0)+P(1)=3e^{-2}$. Ab 1 se ghatao. Trap: $1-P(X\le2)$ lena — wo $X\ge3$ hai; aur sirf $P(X=2)$ dena bhi galat.
ps-tail-direction-03: 'At most 1 defect' $=X\le1$: $X=0$ ya $X=1$. Boundary 1 shaamil hai, 2 nahi.
$e^{-1.5}\approx0.2231$ (yahi $P(X=0)$ hai). Ab $P(X=1)$ jodo. Trap: sirf $P(0)$ pe ruk jaana, ya ulta $P(X\ge2)$ nikal dena.
ps-tail-direction-04: 'No more than 3 failures' — failures 3 se zyada nahi ho sakte. Socho: kaun si values allowed hain, aur kya 3 khud allowed hai?
Translation: 'at most / no more than $k$' → $\le k$; 'fewer than $k$' → $<k$; 'at least $k$' → $\ge k$; 'more than $k$' → $>k$.
Allowed values list karo: 0, 1, 2, ... kahan tak? Phir option match karo. Trap: boundary 3 ko chhod dena, ya complement 'more than 3' chun lena.
ps-tail-direction-05: '$X\ge2$' = 2, 3, 4, 5 — chaar terms. Complement mein sirf $X=0$ aur $X=1$ aate hain, wo aasaan hai.
$P(0)=0.8^5=0.32768$. Ab $P(1)$ nikal ke dono ko 1 se ghatao. Trap: complement $X\le2$ tak le jaana — $X\ge2$ ka complement $X\le1$ par rukta hai.
ps-poisson-rate-01: Rate per hour diya hai par interval 20 minute ka — pehle units match karo. 'No email' = $P(X=0)$.
20 minute $=\frac13$ hour, to $\lambda=6\cdot\frac13$. Ab $e^{-\lambda}$ nikalo. Trap: $\lambda=6$ rakh ke $e^{-6}$, ya $1-e^{-\lambda}$ (at least one) de dena.
ps-poisson-rate-02: $n=500$ bada, $p=0.004$ chhota — Binomial ko Poisson se approximate karo. 'Exactly 2' = $P(X=2)$, $\le2$ nahi.
$\lambda=500\times0.004=2$, aur $e^{-2}\approx0.1353$. Ab $\lambda^2/2!$ se multiply karo. Trap: $2!$ bhool jaana, ya $P(0)+P(1)+P(2)$ jod dena.
ps-poisson-rate-03: 'Average 0.5 per page' ek rate hai aur report 6 pages ki — counts in an interval, to Poisson. Ek page pe ek se zyada typos bhi ho sakte hain.
Units check: (typos/page) × pages = typos — yaani multiply, divide nahi. Ab $\lambda$ nikal ke option dhoondo. Trap: $6/0.5$ karna, ya per-page rate hi poori report ke liye rakh dena.
ps-poisson-rate-04: Rate per hour hai, interval 5 minute — pehle $\lambda$ ko interval pe scale karo. 'At least one' ka complement 'none' hai.
5 minute $=\frac{1}{12}$ hour, to $\lambda=12\cdot\frac1{12}$. Ab $1-e^{-\lambda}$ nikalo. Trap: $e^{-\lambda}$ pe ruk jaana (wo 'none' hai), ya $5/60$ ko hi probability maan lena.
ps-pdf-cdf-01: PDF ki total area 1 honi chahiye — height nahi. $k$ wahi number hai jo $\int_0^2 kx^2\,dx$ ko 1 banaye.
$\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2=\frac{8}{3}$, to equation $\frac{8k}{3}=1$ bani. Ab $k$ solve karo. Trap: $1/3$ factor bhoolna ($8k=1$), ya peak $f(2)=4k$ ko 1 rakhna.
ps-pdf-cdf-02: Pehle $k$ fix karo (area = 1), phir interval probability CDF ke difference se nikalo — density values ka difference nahi.
$\int_0^2(2-x)\,dx=2$, to $k=\frac12$ aur $F(x)=x-\frac{x^2}{4}$. Ab $F(1)$ aur $F(0.5)$ nikal ke ghatao. Trap: sirf $F(1)$ dena, ya $k=1$ maan lena.
ps-pdf-cdf-03: Valid PDF ki do shartein: $[0,2]$ pe har jagah $f(x)\ge0$, aur total area $=1$. Har option dono pe test karo.
Area $=\int_0^2 f(x)\,dx$. Non-negativity ke liye $x=0$ wala end check karo — linear function ka minimum end pe hota hai.
Example: $f(x)=1$ ka area $=2$, to fail. Baaki options ka integral aur $f(0)$ check karo. Trap: sirf area 1 dekh ke ruk jaana — negative values wala function bhi area 1 de sakta hai.
ps-pdf-cdf-04: CDF $F$ diya hai. Teen alag cheezein: density $f=F'$, interval prob $=F(b)-F(a)$, aur continuous $X$ ke liye point prob $=0$.
$F(0.5)=0.5^3=0.125$ — ab har option mein dekho ye kahan lagta hai, aur $F(1)=1$ bhi use karo. Trap: density value $f(0.5)$ ko $P(X=0.5)$ samajhna.
ps-median-cdf-01: Median $m$ wo point hai jahan tak area 0.5 ho: $F(m)=0.5$. Ye $F(0.5)$ evaluate karna nahi hai.
$F(x)=\int_0^x 2t\,dt$; phir $F(m)=0.5$ ko $m$ ke liye solve karo.
$F(x)=x^2$, to equation $m^2=0.5$. Ab positive root lo. Trap: $F(0.5)=0.25$ likh dena, ya mean $\int_0^1 2x^2dx$ de dena.
ps-median-cdf-02: Median $m$: $F(m)=0.5$ solve karna hai. Density $3x^2$ right side pe zyada hai, to median support ke midpoint pe nahi hoga.
$F(x)=x^3$, to $m^3=0.5$ — ab cube root lo. Trap: $F(0.5)=0.125$ dena, mean $3/4$ dena, ya midpoint 0.5 le lena.
ps-median-cdf-03: 'Mean 4' se rate $\lambda=1/4$ hota hai, 4 nahi. Median ke liye $F(m)=0.5$ solve karna hai.
Dono taraf $\ln$ lo: $-m/4=\ln0.5=-\ln2$. Ab $m$ nikalo ($\ln2\approx0.693$). Trap: $\lambda=4$ lena, ya mean ko hi median maan lena — exponential right-skewed hai.
ps-median-cdf-04: Median $m$: jahan tak area 0.5 ho, yaani $F(m)=0.5$. Density badh rahi hai, to median midpoint 2 pe nahi hoga.
$F(x)=\frac{x^2}{16}$, to $\frac{m^2}{16}=0.5$ — ab $m^2$ nikal ke positive root lo. Trap: $F(0.5)$ evaluate karna, ya mean $\int_0^4 x^2/8\,dx$ de dena.
ps-uniform-conditional-01: 'Given $X>4$' — ab $X$ sirf $(4,10)$ mein ho sakta hai, aur wahan bhi uniform hai. Naya sample space yahi interval hai.
Restricted interval $(4,10)$ ki length $=6$. Ab favourable $(7,10)$ ki length nikal ke divide karo. Trap: $7/4$ ya $4/7$ (cut-offs) lena, ya unconditional $3/10$ dena.
ps-uniform-conditional-02: Condition $X>4$ se range $(4,12)$ ban jaati hai. Dono conditions saath lagao: $4<X<6$.
Restricted range $(4,12)$ ki length $=8$. Ab $(4,6)$ ki length isse divide karo. Trap: unconditional $P(X<6)=4/10$, ya joint $2/10$ pe ruk jaana.
ps-uniform-conditional-03: 'Not arrived by minute 10' ek condition hai — ab arrival time $(10,30)$ mein uniform hai. 'Next 10 minutes' = $(10,20)$.
Restricted interval ki length $=30-10=20$. Ab $(10,20)$ ki length se divide karo. Trap: denominator 30 rakhna (unconditional), ya $P(X>10)$ hi de dena.
ps-uniform-conditional-04: Do conditions: $X^2<1$ matlab $-1<X<1$, aur given $X>0$. Restricted space $(0,3)$ hai.
Denominator: $(0,3)$ ki length 3. Ab $(-1,1)$ ka wo hissa jo $X>0$ mein aata hai, uski length nikalo. Trap: poora $(-1,1)$ (length 2) gin lena, ya joint $P(0<X<1)$ pe ruk jaana.
ps-exponential-01: Mean 5 years se rate $\lambda=1/5$ per year — mean khud rate nahi hai. 'More than 5 years' = survival $P(X>5)$.
Exponent $\lambda t=\frac15\times5$ — ab $e^{-\lambda t}$ nikalo. Trap: $1-e^{-\lambda t}$ dena (wo $P(X<5)$ hai), ya mean ko median maan ke 0.5 kehna.
ps-exponential-02: Bulb 600 h pehle hi chal chuka hai — ye 'given' condition hai. Exponential ki khaas property socho: kya purani age future survival ko affect karti hai?
Exponent $=-\lambda t=-500/1000$; ab $e^{\text{exponent}}$ calculate karo. Trap: $e^{-0.6}$ (sirf condition) ya $e^{-1.1}$ (condition ignore) mat lo.
ps-exponential-03: $N=\lfloor X\rfloor=2$ ka matlab $X$ exactly 2 nahi, balki ek poora interval hai. Continuous $X$ ke liye ek point ki probability 0 hoti hai.
$e^{-2(0.5)}=e^{-1}\approx0.3679$; ab $e^{-1.5}$ nikal ke subtract karo. Trap: density $f(2)=0.5e^{-1}$ probability nahi hai, aur $P(X\ge2)$ pe mat ruko.
ps-exponential-04: Mean 2 diya hai — pehle rate nikalo, phir chaaron statements (floor, memoryless, rate, variance) ko alag-alag check karo.
Rules: $\lambda=1/\text{mean}$, $\mathrm{Var}=1/\lambda^2$, $P(X>s+t\mid X>s)=P(X>t)$, aur $\lfloor X\rfloor\sim$ Geometric with $p=1-e^{-\lambda}$.
Variance ke liye $1/\lambda^2$ mein apna $\lambda$ daalo; memoryless wale mein $s=1$ aur $s+t=3$ se $t$ nikalo. Trap: exponential mein mean, SD aur variance ko mix mat karo.
ps-exponential-05: Tail probability $P(X>2)$ di hai, aur mean poocha hai. Pehle tail formula se rate $\lambda$ nikalo, phir mean.
Dono side $\ln$ lo: $2\lambda=\ln 4$, to $\lambda=\ln4/2$. Trap: $\lambda$ ko hi answer mat likh do — mean uska reciprocal hai.
ps-standardize-01: Notation $N(50,16)$ mein 16 variance hai, SD nahi. Aur $P(X>58)$ right tail hai.
$z=(58-50)/4$ calculate karo aur given $\Phi$ value use karo. Trap: 16 se divide karke $z=0.5$ mat lo, aur $\Phi(z)$ hi mat likho — wo left tail hai.
ps-standardize-02: $Y=3Z-2$ standard normal ka linear transformation hai; $Z$ ka mean 0 aur variance 1 hai.
Pehle mean: $3\cdot0-2$. Ab variance ke liye socho shift $-2$ ka koi effect hai kya. Trap: $E[Z]$ ko 1 maanna, ya variance ko $a$ se (not $a^2$) scale karna.
ps-standardize-03: Do-sided interval $85<X<130$ hai, to dono ends standardise karne padenge. $15^2$ variance hai, to $\sigma=15$.
$z_1=-1$, $z_2=2$. Ab $\Phi(-1)=1-0.8413$ nikalo aur $\Phi(2)$ se subtract karo. Trap: $-1$ ko $+1$ maan ke $\Phi(2)-\Phi(1)$ mat karo.
ps-standardize-04: $P(X<40)=0.5$ — normal mein kaunsa point exactly aadha area deta hai? Aur $0.8413=\Phi(1)$ ek $z$-value bata raha hai.
Normal symmetric hai, to median $=\mu$. Phir 46 pe $z=1$: $(46-\mu)/\sigma=1$.
$\mu=40$ daalo: $(46-40)/\sigma=1$ se $\sigma$ nikalo. Trap: question variance maang raha hai, $\sigma$ pe mat ruko.
ps-standardize-05: $E[(2Z+1)^2]$ ek second moment hai, $(E[2Z+1])^2$ nahi. Square ko expand karo ya variance + mean² wala rule lagao.
Term by term: $E[4Z^2]=4\cdot1$, $E[4Z]=0$; ab constant term jodo. Trap: $1^2$ drop mat karo, aur coefficient 2 ko square karna mat bhoolo.
ps-chi-square-01: $Z^2$ ka variance poocha hai, mean nahi. $\mathrm{Var}(Z^2)$ ke liye $Z$ ka 4th moment chahiye.
$(E[Z^2])^2$ nikalo aur $E[Z^4]$ se subtract karo. Trap: $E[Z^4]$ ko hi answer mat likho, aur $E[Z^2]$ (mean of $\chi^2_1$) se confuse mat ho.
ps-chi-square-02: $X_i\sim N(0,4)$ standard normal nahi hain, to $\chi^2_3$ ka '$2k$' seedha nahi lagega. Pehle $X_i$ ko $Z_i$ mein likho.
$X_i=2Z_i$, to $X_i^2=4Z_i^2$; $\mathrm{Var}(cY)=c^2\mathrm{Var}(Y)$ aur $\mathrm{Var}(Z_i^2)=2$. Independent terms ke variances add hote hain.
Ek term: $\mathrm{Var}(4Z_1^2)=4^2\cdot2$. Ab teeno terms ke liye jodo. Trap: sirf 4 se scale karna (not $4^2$), ya mean $3\times4$ de dena.
ps-chi-square-03: $\chi^2_3$ ki definition yaad karo: kitne independent squared standard normals, aur kaise combine? Har option mein dekho square kahan laga hai.
$\chi^2_k=\sum_{i=1}^k Z_i^2$ with $Z_i$ iid $N(0,1)$. Normals ka sum normal hi rehta hai; $cZ^2$ sirf scaled $\chi^2_1$ hai.
$(Z_1+Z_2+Z_3)^2$ check karo: andar $N(0,3)$ hai, standard nahi — to ye $3\chi^2_1$ hai. Baaki options isi tarah check karo. Trap: sirf mean 3 hona kaafi nahi.
ps-chi-square-04: Chaar statements: $V$ ka mean, variance, $Z^2+V$ ka distribution, aur $t$ ki definition. Har ek ko $\chi^2_k$ rules se check karo, $k=4$.
$\chi^2_k$: mean $k$, variance $2k$; independent chi-squares ki df add hoti hai; $t_k=Z/\sqrt{V/k}$.
$Z^2\sim\chi^2_1$, to $Z^2+V$ ki df $=1+4$ — statement se milao. Baaki teen mein $k=4$ daalo. Trap: variance ko $k$ maan lena.
ps-joint-pmf-01: Constant $c$ fix karna hai: saare 6 cells ki probabilities ka total 1 hona chahiye. Lekin har cell ka weight $x+y$ hai, 1 nahi.
Row $x=0$: $0+1+2=3$. Ab row $x=1$ ka sum nikalo, dono jodo, aur $c=1/\text{total}$. Trap: 6 cells gin ke $c=1/6$ mat lo.
ps-joint-pmf-02: 'Given $Y=1$' — sample space sirf $Y=1$ wale cells tak restrict ho jaata hai. Denominator $P(Y=1)$ hoga.
$p(0,1)=1/9$, $p(1,1)=2/9$; ab $P(Y=1)$ jodo aur divide karo. Trap: $P(X=1)=6/9$ se divide mat karo — wo ulta conditional deta hai.
ps-joint-pmf-03: $P(Y=1)$ ek marginal hai — table mein $Y=1$ wala column dekho, row nahi.
Column $Y=1$ ke dono cells (upar se neeche) padho aur jodo. Trap: row $X=1$ jodna (wo $P(X=1)$ hai), ya sirf ek cell $p(1,1)$ le lena.
ps-joint-pmf-04: 'Given $Y=1$' — sirf $Y=1$ column pe dhyan do aur use ek naya mini-distribution banao. $X$ yahan sirf 0 ya 1 ho sakta hai.
$P(Y=1)=0.7$. Ab $p(0,1)/0.7$ aur $p(1,1)/0.7$ banao, phir $\sum x\,P(X=x\mid Y=1)$ lo. Trap: $P(X=1)=0.6$ se divide karna, ya joint cell ko hi conditional maan lena.
ps-joint-pmf-05: Table se pehle marginals nikalo (row sums, column sums). Independence, covariance aur dono conditionals sab inhi se judge honge.
Independent iff har cell $p(x,y)=P(X=x)P(Y=y)$; independent ⇒ Cov $=0$; $P(A\mid B)=p(\text{cell})/P(B)$.
$P(X=1)=0.4$, $P(Y=1)=0.3$: $0.4\times0.3$ ko cell 0.12 se milao, phir baaki cells. Conditionals mein denominator 'given' wala marginal hai. Trap: joint cell ko hi conditional maan lena.
ps-uniform-area-01: Do independent uniforms, alag ranges: $X\in[0,2]$, $Y\in[0,1]$. Probability = favourable area / rectangle area; yahan symmetry se $\frac12$ nahi milega.
Rectangle $[0,2]\times[0,1]$ ka area 2. Region $X\ge Y$ line $y=x$ ke neeche hai; ulta region $X<Y$ ek chhota triangle hai.
$X<Y$ triangle: vertices $(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)$, area $\frac12$. Ise 2 se divide karo, phir complement lo. Trap: $P(X<Y)$ hi report kar dena.
ps-uniform-area-02: $X,Y$ iid $U(0,1)$: unit square pe probability = area. $X+Y\le0.6$ origin wale corner pe ek chhota region hai.
Region line $x+y=0.6$ ke neeche: right triangle, dono legs 0.6. Area $=\frac12\cdot\text{leg}^2$, aur total area 1.
Legs $0.6$ aur $0.6$, to $\text{leg}^2=0.36$ — ab triangle formula complete karo. Trap: $\frac12$ bhoolna, ya $X+Y$ ko uniform maan ke 0.6 de dena.
ps-uniform-area-03: Unit square pe $|X-Y|\le0.2$ diagonal $y=x$ ke around ek band hai. Band ka area seedha mushkil hai — bahar wala hissa easy hai.
Band ke bahar do corner triangles: $y>x+0.2$ aur $y<x-0.2$, dono ki legs $1-0.2=0.8$. $P=1-(\text{dono triangles ka area})$.
Ek triangle ka area $=0.8^2/2$; dono ka total nikal ke 1 se ghatao. Trap: complement hi report karna, ya width $2\times0.2$ × length 1 lena (corners clipped hain).
ps-uniform-area-04: $X\in[0,1]$, $Y\in[0,3]$ — ranges alag hain, to $\frac12$ wali symmetry nahi lagegi. Area method lagao.
Rectangle $[0,1]\times[0,3]$ ka area 3. Region $Y<X$: line $y=x$ ke neeche, $x$ 0 se 1 tak.
$Y<X$ region triangle hai vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)$ — iska area nikalo aur 3 se divide karo. Trap: triangle area mein $\frac12$ bhoolna, ya ulta $P(Y\ge X)$ de dena.
ps-uniform-area-05: $X,Y$ iid $U(0,4)$: square $[0,4]^2$, area 16. Line $y=x/2$ hai, $y=x$ nahi — to region aadha nahi hoga.
$X\ge2Y\iff y\le x/2$. Favourable area $=\int_0^4 \frac{x}{2}\,dx$, phir 16 se divide.
Ye region triangle hai vertices $(0,0),(4,0),(4,2)$; area $=\frac12\cdot4\cdot2$. Ab 16 se divide karo. Trap: ulta region $X<2Y$ ka area le lena.
ps-total-expectation-01: Do groups alag sizes ke hain (60% vs 40%) — overall mean simple average nahi, weighted average hoga.
Regular part: $0.6\times500=300$. Ab new part nikal ke jodo. Trap: 500 aur 200 ka seedha average, ya weights swap kar dena.
ps-total-expectation-02: Tosses ki ginti $k$ khud random hai (die se aati hai). Pehle fixed $k$ pe expected heads socho, phir $k$ pe average karo.
To $E[H]=\frac12E[k]$; fair die ke liye $E[k]=(1+2+\dots+6)/6$. Ise compute karke half karo. Trap: $E[k]$ ko hi answer de dena.
ps-total-expectation-03: $E[X\mid Y]=2Y+1$ abhi bhi $Y$ pe depend karta hai — $E[X]$ ek number hai, to $Y$ pe average karna padega.
$Y\sim U(0,1)$ ka mean $(0+1)/2$ hai; ise $2E[Y]+1$ mein daalo. Trap: $Y=0$ ya $Y=1$ plug kar dena — average karna hai.
ps-total-expectation-04: Route ke hisaab se mean time alag hai aur route ki probability bhi alag — isliye weighted average chahiye.
Pehla term: $\frac13\cdot30=10$. Ab doosra term nikal ke jodo. Trap: 30 aur 15 ka unweighted average, weights swap, ya dono means seedha jodna.
ps-total-variance-01: Random member ka variance do jagah se aata hai: group ke andar ka spread, aur group means (10 vs 20) ke beech ka farak.
$\mathrm{Var}(X)=E[\mathrm{Var}(X\mid G)]+\mathrm{Var}(E[X\mid G])$; dono groups ki probability $\frac12$.
Within part: $\frac12(4)+\frac12(4)=4$. Between part: means 10, 20 (equally likely) ka variance $E[M^2]-(E[M])^2$ nikalo, phir jodo. Trap: sirf ek part rakhna, ya $4+4$ jodna.
ps-total-variance-02: Ye mixture hai: prob 0.4 pe $N(0,1)$, prob 0.6 pe $N(5,4)$. Variance = within-component part + between-means part.
Within $=2.8$ aur $\mu=3$. Ab between part $0.4(9)+0.6(4)$ nikal ke within mein jodo. Trap: $N(5,4)$ mein 4 variance hai, SD nahi; aur sirf within pe mat ruko.
ps-total-variance-03: Formula ke ek term ka meaning poocha hai. $E[\mathrm{Var}(X\mid Y)]$ ko andar se bahar padho: pehle Var, phir $E$.
Andar: $\mathrm{Var}(X\mid Y=y)$ = sirf group $y$ ke members ka spread. Bahar ka $E$ us spread ko $Y$ ke groups pe average karta hai. $\mathrm{Var}(E[X\mid Y])$ = group means ka spread.
Dono terms non-negative hain aur unka sum $\mathrm{Var}(X)$ hai — to koi ek term total se bada ho sakta hai kya? Options isi se judge karo. Trap: 'within' aur 'between' ulta samajhna.
ps-total-variance-04: Ye 'any $X,Y$' wala conceptual sawaal hai — har statement ko total variance formula ke structure se check karo: dono parts add hote hain ya multiply?
$\mathrm{Var}(X)=E[\mathrm{Var}(X\mid Y)]+\mathrm{Var}(E[X\mid Y])$, aur dono terms $\ge0$ hain.
Har special case mein dekho kaunsa term 0 banta hai: $E[X\mid Y]$ constant ho to constant ka variance? $X=g(Y)$ ho to $Y$ diya hone pe $X$ ka spread? Trap: '+' ko '×' padh lena.
ps-total-variance-05: $X$ ka mean khud random $N$ pe depend karta hai — total variance formula lagega. Poisson ki khaas property yaad karo: mean aur variance ka relation.
$N$ uniform on $\{1,2,3\}$: $E[N]=2$. Ab $\mathrm{Var}(N)=E[N^2]-2^2$ with $E[N^2]=(1+4+9)/3$ nikalo aur jodo. Trap: sirf ek part rakhna.
ps-descriptive-01: Old mean 9 values ka hai, aur ek naya value 30 aaya. Mean ko seedha average mat karo — totals ke through jao.
Old total $=180$. Ab 30 jodo aur 10 se divide karo. Trap: $(20+30)/2$ — old mean 9 values represent karta hai, 1 nahi.
ps-descriptive-02: Median ke liye data pehle sort karna zaroori hai. Yahan $n=6$ (even) hai.
Even $n$: median = sorted data ke 3rd aur 4th values ka average.
Sort karo: 2, 2, 5, … — baaki list poori karo, phir 3rd aur 4th ka average lo. Trap: unsorted list ke beech wale values lena, ya mean/mode se confuse karna.
ps-descriptive-03: Ek value galat record hua (40 ki jagah 10) — to total galat hai. Mean ko seedha nahi, total ko correct karo.
Old total $=300$. Galat 10 hatao, sahi 40 jodo, phir 20 se divide karo. Trap: correction ulti direction mein lagana, ya poora 30 mean mein jod dena (mean mein sirf $30/20$ judta hai).
ps-descriptive-04: Sirf extreme value 10 → 100 badla hai. Har measure ke liye socho: kya wo value ke size pe depend karta hai, ya sirf position/frequency pe?
Mean $=\text{total}/n$; range $=\max-\min$; median = sorted middle value; mode = sabse frequent value.
Total change $=100-10=90$ aur $n=5$ — mean ka change nikalo. Naya sorted data 2, 4, 4, 5, 100 likh ke baaki teen check karo. Trap: range $=\max-\min$ hai, sirf max nahi.
ps-covariance-01: Teen moments diye hain: $E[X]$, $E[Y]$, $E[XY]$ — covariance ka shortcut formula seedha lagega.
$E[X]E[Y]=2\cdot3=6$; ab ise $E[XY]$ se subtract karo. Trap: $E[XY]$ ko hi answer de dena, ya ulta subtract karna.
ps-covariance-02: Correlation ke liye covariance ko SDs ke product se divide karte hain — yahan variances diye hain, SDs nahi.
$\sigma_X\sigma_Y=3\cdot4=12$; ab Cov 6 ko isse divide karo. Trap: $9\cdot16$ ya $9+16$ se divide karna.
ps-covariance-03: Linear combination $2X-3Y$ ka variance hai, aur Cov negative hai — coefficients square honge aur cross term ka sign dhyan se.
$a^2\sigma_X^2=4\cdot4=16$, $b^2\sigma_Y^2=9\cdot9=81$. Ab $2(2)(-3)(-2)$ ka sign carefully nikalo aur jodo. Trap: cross term drop karna, ya do negatives ka sign galat lena.
ps-covariance-04: Covariance chahiye, correlation nahi. Table se $E[X]$, $E[Y]$ aur $E[XY]$ nikalo.
$\mathrm{Cov}=E[XY]-E[X]E[Y]$. $XY$ sirf cell $(1,1)$ pe non-zero hai, to $E[XY]=p(1,1)$.
$E[X]=P(X=1)=0.2+0.4=0.6$, $E[Y]=P(Y=1)=0.3+0.4=0.7$. Ab product nikal ke $E[XY]$ se subtract karo. Trap: order ulta lena, ya $\sigma_X\sigma_Y$ se divide kar dena.
ps-covariance-05: 'Independent' word dekho — ye covariance ke baare mein kya batata hai? Aur $X-Y$ mein $Y$ ka coefficient $-1$ hai.
$(-1)^2=1$, to $\mathrm{Var}Y$ plus sign ke saath aata hai. Ab values daalo. Trap: $3-5$ karna — variance kabhi negative nahi hota.
ps-cov-independence-01: $Y=X^2$ — $Y$ poori tarah $X$ se fix hai, lekin relation linear nahi (U-shape). Dependence aur covariance alag cheezein hain.
$X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equally likely: $E[X]=0$, $E[X^3]=(-1+0+1)/3$ — Cov nikalo. Phir $P(Y=0)$ ko $P(Y=0\mid X=0)=1$ se compare karo. Trap: Cov $=0$ se independence maan lena.
ps-cov-independence-02: Chaar implications hain — 'Cov 0' aur 'independent' ke beech kaunsi direction always hold karti hai? Har statement ko implication + contrapositive ki tarah dekho.
Pakka rule: independent ⇒ $E[XY]=E[X]E[Y]$ ⇒ Cov $=0$. Koi implication sahi ho to uska contrapositive bhi sahi; converse zaroori nahi.
Counterexample: $X$ uniform on $\{-1,0,1\}$, $Y=X^2$ — Cov 0 hai par dependent. Ise har statement pe lagao. Trap: converse ko bhi true maan lena.
ps-cov-independence-03: Chaar points symmetric hain aur har point pe ya $X=0$ ya $Y=0$. Do cheezein alag-alag check karo: Cov, aur independence.
Cov $=E[XY]-E[X]E[Y]$. Independence ke liye har pair pe $P(X=x,Y=y)=P(X=x)P(Y=y)$ chahiye.
Har point pe $XY=0$, aur symmetry se $E[X]=E[Y]=0$ — Cov nikalo. Phir $P(X=0)$, $P(Y=0)$ aur $P(X=0,Y=0)$ compare karo. Trap: Cov 0 dekh ke independence maan lena.
ps-cov-independence-04: Chaar statements: $N(0,1)$ ke liye $\mathrm{Cov}(X,X^2)$, jointly normal ka special case, $\rho=0$ ka matlab, aur $X$ vs $X^2$ ki independence. Har ek alag judge karo.
$\mathrm{Cov}(X,X^2)=E[X^3]-E[X]E[X^2]$. General rule: Cov 0 ⇏ independence; sirf jointly normal mein Cov 0 ⇒ independent. $\rho$ sirf linear association naapta hai.
$N(0,1)$ symmetric hai — odd moments $E[X]$, $E[X^3]$ kya honge? Cov mein daalo. Phir socho: $X$ jaan ke kya $X^2$ fix ho jaata hai? Trap: $\rho=0$ ko 'koi relation nahi' padhna.
ps-clt-sum-01: Sum $S$ ka SD poocha hai (mean ka SE nahi). Yaad rakho: independent terms ke variances add hote hain, SDs nahi.
$\sqrt{25}=5$; ab ise $\sigma=3$ se multiply karo. Trap: SD ko $n$ se multiply karna ($3\times25$), ya variance hi report kar dena.
ps-clt-sum-02: Sample mean ka standard error chahiye — population $\sigma$ ko sample size ke hisaab se chhota karna hai.
$\sqrt{36}=6$; ab divide karo. Trap: $n$ se divide karna, ya $\sigma^2/n$ (jo $\bar X$ ka variance hai) de dena.
ps-clt-sum-03: 400 tosses mein heads Binomial$(400,0.5)$ hai; normal approximation ke liye pehle mean aur SD nikalo. '$\ge220$' right tail hai.
$np=200$, $np(1-p)=100$, to SD $=10$. Ab $z$ nikalo aur right tail lo. Trap: variance 100 ko SD maan ke $z=0.2$ lena, ya $\Phi(z)$ hi report karna.
ps-clt-sum-04: Sawaal $\bar X$ ke baare mein hai, ek $X$ ke nahi — CLT se $\bar X$ approx normal hai, par chhote spread ke saath. Variance 4 diya hai, SD nahi.
$SE=2/10=0.2$. Ab $z=0.4/0.2$ nikalo aur right tail $1-\Phi(z)$ lo. Trap: $\sigma^2/n=0.04$ ko SE lena, ya $\sqrt n$ bhool ke $\sigma=2$ use karna.
ps-ci-compute-01: $\sigma$ known hai, to $z$-interval. Sirf upper limit chahiye — ek number, poora interval nahi.
$SE=16/8=2$. Ab $1.96\times SE$ nikal ke 50 mein jodo. Trap: $\sqrt n$ bhoolna, $n$ se divide karna, ya minus karke lower limit de dena.
ps-ci-compute-02: 'Total width' poocha hai — ye margin of error (half-width) ka double hai. $\sigma$ known hai, to $z$-interval.
$SE=10/\sqrt{100}=1$, to margin $=1.96\times1$. Ab total width ke liye last step karo. Trap: margin of error pe ruk jaana, ya $\sigma/n$ use karna.
ps-ci-compute-03: Margin of error $\le1$ chahiye aur $n$ dhoondhna hai — inequality ko $n$ ke liye solve karo. 'Smallest $n$' ek integer hona chahiye.
$1.96\times5=9.8$; ab $9.8^2$ nikalo. Trap: decimal ko round down karna — tab margin 1 se thoda upar chala jaata hai; aur square karna mat bhoolo.
ps-ci-compute-04: $\sigma$ unknown hai aur $n=16$ chhota — $t$-interval lagega, $z$ nahi. Teen critical values diye hain; sahi wala chuno.
CI $=\bar x\pm t_{0.025,\,n-1}\cdot s/\sqrt n$, with df $=n-1=15$.
$SE=8/\sqrt{16}=2$, aur multiplier $t_{0.025,15}=2.131$. Ab margin nikal ke $20\pm$ margin karo. Trap: df $=16$ ya $z=1.96$ use kar lena.
ps-ci-interpret-01: Ek computed interval $(12.1,\ 15.3)$ hai. Har statement mein dekho probability kis pe lagayi ja rahi hai — fixed $\mu$ pe, procedure pe, ya individual observations pe?
Interval $\bar x\pm\text{margin}$ symmetric hai, to centre $=\bar x$. '95%' procedure ki long-run coverage hai; $\mu$ fixed hai, random nahi.

Centre $=(12.1+15.3)/2$ nikalo aur statement se milao. Baaki ke liye poochho: fixed $\mu$ ko probability di ja rahi hai, ya CI ko observations pe lagaya ja raha hai? Trap: computed interval ke baad $\mu$ pe probability lagana.
ps-ci-interpret-02: Width $\sigma$, $n$ aur confidence level pe depend karti hai. Har statement mein ek cheez badal rahi hai — dekho width kaise react karti hai.
Quadrupling: $\sqrt{4n}=2\sqrt n$ — width ka factor kya hoga? Baaki statements formula ke numerator/denominator se check karo. Trap: width ko $1/n$ ke proportional maan lena (wo $1/\sqrt n$ hai).
ps-ci-interpret-03: Interval already compute ho chuka hai. Socho: $\mu$ random hai ya fixed? Aur '90%' kis cheez ki property hai?
Frequentist rule: $\mu$ fixed constant hai; 90% = procedure repeat karne pe kitne intervals $\mu$ ko cover karenge. Computed interval ke liye $\mu$ pe probability statement nahi banta.
Har option mein dekho probability kis pe lagi hai: $\mu$, future $\bar x$, ya method. Aur $\bar x$ to interval ka centre hai — kya wo bahar ho sakta hai? Trap: fixed $\mu$ ko probability dena.
ps-ci-interpret-04: CI $(48,\ 56)$ aur 5% two-sided test ek hi cheez ke do roop hain (CI–test duality). Har $\mu_0$ ke liye dekho wo interval ke andar hai ya bahar.
Margin = half-width $=(\text{upper}-\text{lower})/2$. Duality: $\mu_0$ 95% CI ke bahar ⇔ 5% pe reject; andar ⇔ fail to reject.
$(56-48)/2$ nikalo aur margin wale statement se milao. Phir 58 aur 50 ko interval pe place karo. Trap: CI ya test se '$H_0$ true hone ki probability' nikaal lena.
ps-test-select-01: Teen sawaal poochho: parameter kya hai (mean ya variance)? $\sigma$ known ya unknown? Aur $n=12$ chhota hai.
Mean, $\sigma$ unknown, normal sample → $t$ with $n-1$ df. $\chi^2_{n-1}$ variance ke liye hai; $z$ ke liye $\sigma$ known chahiye.
Yahan $n=12$ hai — df $=n-1$ nikalo aur options se milao. Trap: df $=n$ le lena.
ps-test-select-02: $H_0$ variance ($\sigma^2=4$) ke baare mein hai, mean ke baare mein nahi — to mean wale $t$/$z$ statistics yahan kaam ke nahi.
Normal population ka variance test: $\chi^2=(n-1)s^2/\sigma_0^2\sim\chi^2_{n-1}$ under $H_0$.

Options mein dekho kaunsa statistic $s^2$ use karta hai aur kaunsa $\bar x$; phir $\sigma_0^2=4$ daal ke milao. Trap: $\sum(O-E)^2/E$ ko variance test samajhna — wo counts (goodness-of-fit) ke liye hai.
ps-test-select-03: $\chi^2$ test kab lagta hai? Har situation mein dekho data kis type ka hai (counts/table vs measurements) aur parameter kya hai (mean vs variance).
$\chi^2$ ke teen use: goodness of fit (counts), independence ($r\times c$ table), aur ek normal variance ($(n-1)s^2/\sigma_0^2$). Mean ke liye $z$/$t$.
Har option ko in buckets mein daalo: height ka mean, die ke counts, $2\times3$ table, variance 9. Trap: sirf 'normal' ya '$\sigma$' word dekh ke test chunna — pehle parameter dekho.
ps-test-select-04: Mean ka test hai, $\sigma$ unknown, aur sample SD $s=6$ diya hai — $t$ statistic. Denominator SE hai, sirf $s$ nahi.
Numerator $=2$ aur $SE=6/4=1.5$. Ab divide karo. Trap: $\sqrt n$ bhoolna ($2/6$), ya $s/n$ le lena.
ps-test-select-05: Goodness-of-fit: fair coin ke under har cell (heads, tails) ka expected count nikalo, phir dono cells ka contribution jodo.
$\chi^2=\sum\frac{(O-E)^2}{E}$ with $E=100\times0.5$ for heads aur tails dono.
Heads cell: $(60-50)^2/50=100/50$. Ab tails cell ka term nikal ke jodo. Trap: sirf ek cell lena, ya $E^2$ se divide karna.
ps-test-logic-01: $p=0.03$ diya hai. Statements do type ke hain: decision ($\alpha=0.05$ aur $0.01$ pe) aur p-value ka meaning — dono alag check karo.
Reject $H_0$ iff $p\le\alpha$. p-value $=P(\text{data at least this extreme}\mid H_0\text{ true})$ — ye $H_0$ ki probability nahi hai.
0.03 ko pehle 0.05 se, phir 0.01 se compare karo aur har case ka decision likho. Trap: p-value ko '$P(H_0$ true$)$' padhna.
ps-test-logic-02: $p=0.12$ aur $\alpha=0.05$ — pehle compare karo, phir decision ki wording dhyan se padho.
Rule: reject iff $p\le\alpha$; warna 'fail to reject' — 'accept' ya '$H_0$ proved' nahi bolte, aur $p$ $H_0$ ki probability nahi hai.
$0.12$ vs $0.05$: kaunsa bada hai? Us hisaab se decision lo, phir wo option dhoondo jiski wording bhi sahi ho. Trap: 'accept $H_0$' ya '12% chance $H_0$ true' jaisi wording.
ps-test-logic-03: Two-sided test hai — p-value mein dono tails count honge. $\Phi(1.8)$ left side ka area hai.
Ek tail: $1-0.9641=0.0359$. Ab two-sided ke liye last step karo. Trap: one-sided pe ruk jaana, ya $\Phi(1.8)$ ko hi p-value maan lena.
ps-test-logic-04: $H_1:\mu>\mu_0$ right-tailed hai, par observed $z=-1.5$ negative hai — data $H_1$ ki ulti direction mein hai. Tail $H_1$ decide karta hai, $z$ ka sign nahi.
Right-tailed: $p=P(Z\ge z_{obs})$ with $z_{obs}=-1.5$, chahe $z$ negative ho.
Sketch: $-1.5$ ke right ka area 0.5 se bada hai ya chhota? Symmetry $P(Z\ge-a)=P(Z\le a)$ se given $\Phi$ use karo. Trap: $z$ negative dekh ke left tail le lena.
ps-errors-power-01: Type II error ki definition: actually kaunsi hypothesis true hai, aur test ne kya decide kiya?
Type I = $H_0$ true hote hue galat decision (prob $\alpha$). Type II = $H_1$ true hote hue galat decision (prob $\beta$).

Har option ko (truth, decision) pair mein likho: $H_1$ true ho to kaunsa decision galat hai? Jo sahi decision hai wo error nahi. Trap: Type I/II ulta karna, ya error ko '$H_0$ false hone ki probability' samajhna.
ps-errors-power-02: Power $H_1$ ke under nikalti hai ($\mu=2$), $H_0$ ke under nahi. Rejection region $X>1.5$ hai.
$z=-0.5$, to power $=P(Z>-0.5)$. Sketch: $-0.5$ ke right ka area 0.5 se bada hai — ise given $\Phi$ values se likho. Trap: $\mu=0$ use karna (wo $\alpha$ deta hai), ya $\beta$ report karna.
ps-errors-power-03: Chaar statements $\alpha$, $\beta$, power aur $n$ ke relation pe hain. Har ek ke liye socho: ye probability kis hypothesis ke under calculate hoti hai?
$\alpha=P(\text{reject}\mid H_0)$, $\beta=P(\text{not reject}\mid H_1)$, power $=1-\beta=P(\text{reject}\mid H_1)$. $\alpha$ aur $\beta$ alag hypotheses ke under hain.
$\alpha$ 0.05→0.01: rejection region chhota hoga — $H_1$ ke under miss zyada ya kam? Bada $n$ → SE chhota → distributions ka overlap? Trap: '$\alpha+\beta=1$' jaisi identity maan lena.
ps-errors-power-04: Type I error = $H_0$ (fair coin) true hote hue reject karna. Rejection tab hota hai jab 5 tosses sab same hon — aur 'same' ke do tarike hain.
$(1/2)^5=1/32$. Ab dono cases jodo aur decimal mein likho. Trap: sirf all-heads ginna, ya $1-\alpha$ de dena.
ps-estimator-01: Do alag cheezein check karni hain: unbiasedness ($E[\hat\theta]=\theta$?) aur variance. Har estimator ka pehle expected value nikalo.
Linearity: $E[\frac1n\sum X_i]=\frac1n\sum E[X_i]$. $\mathrm{Var}(cY)=c^2\mathrm{Var}(Y)$ aur independent terms add. Sample variance unbiased tabhi hota hai jab divisor $n-1$ ho.
$\mathrm{Var}(\bar X)=\frac{1}{n^2}\cdot n\sigma^2$ simplify karke statement se milao; $X_1$ ke liye bas $E[X_1]$ dekho. Trap: 'unbiased' aur 'kam variance' ko ek hi cheez samajhna.
ps-estimator-02: Unbiased ka matlab $E[T]=\mu$. $T$ ek weighted sum hai — weights 1, 2, 3.
$E[T]=\frac{E[X_1]+2E[X_2]+3E[X_3]}{k}$, aur har $E[X_i]=\mu$; ise $\mu$ ke barabar rakho.
Weights ka sum nikalo aur $\frac{(\text{sum})\,\mu}{k}=\mu$ solve karo. Trap: weights ke squares ka sum lena (wo variance mein aata hai), ya terms ki ginti se divide karna.
ps-estimator-03: Dono estimators unbiased hain par alag number of observations use karte hain — variance compare karni hai. Ratio ka order dekho: $T_2$ upar hai.
Mean of $m$ iid values ka variance $=\sigma^2/m$. $T_1$ mein $m=4$, $T_2$ mein $m=2$.
$\mathrm{Var}(T_1)=\sigma^2/4$. Ab $\mathrm{Var}(T_2)=\frac14(\sigma^2+\sigma^2)$ simplify karo aur ratio lo. Trap: ratio ulta lena, ya 'dono unbiased hain to variance same' maan lena.
ps-estimator-04: $n$ badhne pe $\bar X$ ki do properties dekho: uska mean (bias) aur uska spread (variance). Kaunsi cheez $n$ pe depend karti hai?
$E[\bar X]=\mu$ har $n$ ke liye; $\mathrm{Var}(\bar X)=\sigma^2/n$, aur SE $=\sigma/\sqrt n$.
Statement mein 'Var' likha hai ya 'SE' — $1/n$ aur $1/\sqrt n$ alag rakho. Aur jo already exactly $\mu$ hai, wo 'closer' kaise hoga? Trap: variance aur SE ki rate mix karna.
